verses.text: Elihu went on:
Listen to what I’m saying, you wise men. Hear me out, you who have knowledge.
The ear tests words the way the tongue tastes food.
Let’s decide for ourselves what’s right and work out together what’s good.
Job has said, ‘I’m in the right, but God has denied me justice.
Even though I’m right, I’m treated as a liar. My wound won’t heal, though I haven’t rebelled.’
Who is like Job? He drinks up scorn like water.
He keeps company with people who do wrong and walks with the wicked.
He’s said, ‘What good does it do anyone to take delight in God?’
So listen to me, you who have understanding. It’s unthinkable for God to do evil or for the Almighty to do wrong.
He pays people back for what they’ve done and gives each person what their conduct deserves.
God will never do evil. The Almighty will never twist justice.
Who put him in charge of the earth? Who appointed him over the whole world?
If he turned his attention only to himself and took back his spirit and his breath,
every living thing would die together, and human beings would return to dust.
If you have understanding, hear this. Listen to what I’m saying.
Should someone who hates justice be in charge? Will you condemn the one who is righteous and mighty,
who can say to a king, ‘You’re vile,’ and to nobles, ‘You’re wicked’?
He doesn’t favor rulers or give the rich special treatment over the poor. He made them all with his own hands.
They can die in an instant, even at midnight. People are shaken and pass away. The mighty are swept away without a human hand.
God watches how people live. He sees every step they take.
There’s no darkness or deep shadow where people who do wrong can hide.
God doesn’t need to examine anyone further before calling them before him for judgment.
He shatters the mighty in ways no one can trace and puts others in their place.
He knows what they’ve done. He overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
He strikes them in public for the evil they’ve done,
because they turned away from him and refused to pay attention to his ways.
They made the poor cry out to him, and he heard the cries of people who were suffering.
If God grants peace, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? He rules over nations and individuals alike,
to keep godless people from ruling and laying traps for others.
Has anyone said to God, ‘I’m guilty, and I’ll stop doing wrong.
Teach me what I can’t see. If I’ve done wrong, I won’t do it again’?
Should God repay you on your terms just because you reject his decision? The choice is yours. Tell me what you know.
People with understanding will tell me, and so will every wise person who hears me,
‘Job speaks without knowledge. There’s no wisdom in his words.’
I wish Job’s claims were tested all the way, because he answers like people who do evil.
He adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands in front of us and keeps piling up words against God.
